correctness.rationale: The exact A2 and A4 formulas follow from disk monomial orthogonality applied to P and P^2. The triangle bound on the single mixed coefficient is sharp precisely for affine coefficient phases. The two-variable rational quotient R(u,q) has a strictly increasing-then-decreasing profile in q for every u>=0. Its unique optimum reduces to rational M(u), whose factored derivative has exactly one positive sign-switching cubic root. Boundary c=0 is the separately proved degree-one constant 8/5, and u=0 and infinity are included. Root elimination and equality reconstruction are checked by exact symbolic arithmetic in packaged verify.py; 400 numerical disk quadrature experiments corroborate but do not prove the continuous claim. Kernel obstruction follows from invariant b^2/(ac) for w nonzero and the constant case w=0.

originality.rationale: A nine-query published-finding search and comparisons against relevant published results found no equivalent claim. The mathematically closest accessible published Fourier quadratic result optimizes Euclidean-coefficient L6 on the unit circle, not normalized-area Bergman A2-to-A4; its proof and equality family were read, not merely inferred from title. Primary full texts of arXiv:1701.06897, 2005.14176, 2203.12349, and the theorem in arXiv:2505.12760 concern weighted contracts, sampling, full-space kernel functionals, or a nonsharp fixed-degree inequality; none proves the exact unweighted quadratic constant and kernel obstruction. Priority remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent finite-degree unweighted Bergman ratio may occur as an unstated corollary or table in older approximation literature; negative searches do not certify priority.

value.rationale: The constant is a natural optimal norm of the inclusion of the first nonlinear finite-dimensional Bergman polynomial subspace, equivalently the sharp symmetric-square multiplication concentration factor. Exact low-degree constants benchmark degree-sensitive Nikolskii theory and Gaussian/Bergman concentration. The theorem pinpoints the first finite-degree obstruction to choosing an extremizer from truncated reproducing kernels: kernels work for degree 1 but provably not degree 2. The complete equality geometry and algebraic sharp value are not a mere known-table recomputation or a local random slice. It does not claim a general-degree result or unrelated reconstruction consequences.
